name: internal-linking-auditor
description: Completely free ChatGPT plugin for SEO internal-link audits using uploaded CSVs. No third-party account, external service connection, or website login required.

interface.shortDescription: Free SEO link audits—no external account connections
interface.longDescription: Completely free—no plugin fees or paid upgrades. No external service or website connection required: no third-party account, Search Console authorization, API key, or site login. Upload two Search Console CSV exports directly in ChatGPT; optional Screaming Frog CSVs add detail. Receive an Excel plan with prioritized internal links, anchors, and fixes. Upload the report and a new crawl to verify edits. Files are processed by the plugin's hosted MCP server; it never edits your website.
defaultPrompt: Start an internal linking audit. What website details and Search Console files do you need?
Find the internal links I should add or fix and give me one Excel report with exact instructions.
Check which fixes in my saved Excel report appear in this new crawl.

positive.description: Guide a user who only supplied the website
positive.prompt: Start an internal linking audit for https://example.com. What do you need from me?
positive.expected_behavior: Asks for keyword phrases or a general audit, identifies the two required Search Console CSVs, and explains what the Excel report will contain.

positive.description: Run the basic audit with both CSV attachments
positive.prompt: Audit https://example.com generally using my attached Internal Links and Performance Pages CSVs. Give me one Excel report and explain what I should do first.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns one working Excel link and explains the first actions in workbook order. Treats source suggestions as candidates and reports missing Search Console link counts as unknown.

positive.description: Use crawl and snippet evidence to prioritize exact edits
positive.prompt: Audit https://example.com using my attached CSVs. Focus on heat pump installation and prioritize https://example.com/services/heat-pump-installation. Use the before crawl and snippets. Give me an Excel report with the precise placements and show the evidence.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows two high-priority content placements first in both chat and Excel, with the source, sentence and anchor, plus zero observed main-content sources and nine navigation sources for the priority destination in the supplied crawl.

positive.description: Verify links using the workbook from the previous case
positive.prompt: In the same chat as the crawl and snippets test, reattach its downloaded Excel workbook together with crawl-pages.csv and crawl-inlinks-after.csv from https://github.com/ahmadmohee/internal-linking-auditor/tree/v0.5.6/examples/sprint. Which edits are confirmed?
positive.expected_behavior: Verifies the new content link from the running costs guide, leaves the sizing guide addition open, and provides one updated Excel report.

positive.description: Accept standard Screaming Frog exports with both Status Code and Status, and Destination and Target
positive.prompt: Audit https://example.com using the attached Search Console and full-header Screaming Frog exports. Prioritize the heat pump installation service page and return an Excel plan.
positive.expected_behavior: Parses the numeric Status Code and URL Destination without confusing them with the descriptive Status or HTML Target attribute. Produces two verified placement candidates in the workbook without an ambiguous-column error.

negative.description: Handle a partial crawl without claiming verification
negative.prompt: Verify the edits from my earlier Excel audit for https://example.com. I only have the fresh Internal pages export and I don't have All Inlinks.
negative.expected_behavior: Requests the missing fresh All Inlinks export and the saved workbook if it has not been supplied. Does not mark an edit verified.

publication.release_notes: Fixes Screaming Frog full-export parsing when Internal includes both Status Code and Status or All Inlinks contains Destination and Target. Preserves legacy aliases and adds regression tests; no changes to the MCP endpoint or audit workflow.
